acc_acid = D.acceptance_for(UO, "acidic_variants")[1]

def acceptance_df():
    """Planned acceptance criterion per measured response (basis + criterion)."""
    rows = []
    for r in D.responses(UO):
        lo, hi, stype = D.acceptance_for(UO, r)
        if stype == "lower":
            basis = "Cumulative requirement less the clearance credited to Steps 8 and 9"
            crit = f"≥ {lo:.2f} log₁₀ across the step"
        else:
            ck = r if r in set(cqa_reg["key"]) else D.RESP_TO_CQA.get(r)
            unit = str(cqa_reg[cqa_reg["key"] == ck].iloc[0]["unit"])
            basis = "Drug-substance specification"
            crit = f"≤ {hi:g} {unit}"
        rows.append([D.RESP_LABEL.get(r, r), basis, crit])
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Measured response", "Basis of the criterion",
                                       "Criterion applied to the pool"])

# Purpose and scope

This plan defines the process characterization study for the low-pH viral inactivation
step of the A-Mab drug-substance process. The step is a hold on the Protein A eluate
under acidic conditions, and it is the point in the purification train at which
enveloped virus is inactivated instead of being removed. The study will quantify how the
hold conditions govern virus inactivation and product quality, and it will establish the
operating ranges that the commercial control strategy applies at the receiving site, so
that the ranges carried into commercial manufacture are the ranges this study has
characterized. It is a Stage 1 activity in the lifecycle approach to process validation
[@fda2011], and it follows the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8(R2) [@ichq8].

The scope runs from the point at which the Protein A eluate is titrated to the
inactivation pH to the point at which the held pool is neutralized for cation exchange.
The step has `{python} n_par` parameters in scope, of which `{python} n_mv` will be studied in a
multivariate design and `{python} n_uv` in a univariate assessment, on the basis set out
in §4.3. Every run of the multivariate design will be measured for `{python} n_resp`
responses, namely the XMuLV log reduction factor, the aggregate content of the pool and
the acidic charge variants of the pool.

Three things sit outside this plan. The clearance contributed by the anion exchange and
small-virus retentive filtration steps is characterized in PCP-008 and PCP-009 and is not
evaluated here, although the clearance credited to those steps enters this plan as a
fixed input to the acceptance criterion of §7. The cumulative viral clearance claim for
the drug substance is consolidated in PCMR-001, and no part of that claim is established by this step alone.
Commercial-scale process performance qualification is a Stage 2 activity under PTP-001.

# Objectives

The study has five objectives.

- (i) Quantify the effect of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature on the XMuLV log
  reduction factor, on pool aggregate and on pool acidic variants, over the ranges given
  in §6.
- (ii) Define the multivariate region in which the log reduction factor meets the step
  criterion of §7 while aggregate and acidic variants stay inside their drug-substance
  specifications.
- (iii) Establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter and each governed
  attribute, both at the set-points of the other parameters and with the other parameters
  varying inside their normal operating ranges (§8).
- (iv) Provide the evidence from which each parameter will be classified in PCR-006 under
  SOP-4001.
- (v) Justify the Stage 2 operating ranges for the step and its contribution to the
  control strategy for the drug substance.

This plan states its criteria before any data exist. No operating region, no proven
acceptable range and no parameter classification is asserted here, and every outcome is
reported in PCR-006.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

Low-pH viral inactivation is the second step of the A-Mab purification train and the
first step with a dedicated viral-safety function. The Protein A eluate is already
acidic, so the pool is titrated to the inactivation pH, held for a defined time under
temperature control, and then titrated to the load condition of the cation exchange step,
which places the hold between two chromatography operations and gives it no separating
function of its own. Inactivation is a chemical process and not a separation. Acid
disrupts the lipid envelope and the envelope glycoproteins of susceptible viruses, so infectivity is lost while the
virus particle stays in the pool. Non-enveloped viruses have no envelope to disrupt, and
this step makes no clearance claim for minute virus of mice or for any other
non-enveloped model virus. The claim that is made covers the enveloped model virus
(xenotropic murine leukaemia virus, XMuLV) and is framed by ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a].

The low-pH hold is the most established operation in the purification train. Three
earlier humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) were manufactured with the
same hold, and its process conditions have remained essentially unchanged for those
products and through A-Mab clinical and engineering manufacture [@amab2009]. The
behaviour of the step is understood mechanistically. Inactivation is faster at lower pH,
at longer hold and at higher temperature, so the worst case for viral safety is the top
of the pH range combined with the shortest hold at the lowest temperature, and that
corner is the one the design has to resolve most precisely. Product quality moves in the
opposite direction. The aggregate content of the pool rises with the
length and the temperature of the hold, and acid-induced conformational change of the
antibody adds a further aggregation risk at the low end of the pH scale. The two
mechanisms bound the usable pH window from opposite sides.

The inactivation kinetics established on the prior products transfer directly to A-Mab,
and the low-pH hold is treated here as a settled platform operation. What the study adds
is the bounds of those kinetics over the ranges the commercial process will use. The
commercial control strategy needs the edges of the usable window, so each parameter is expanded beyond its routine control
range and the design is loaded toward those edges. The design is centred between the
edges of the characterization ranges, so the study resolves the region as a whole and not
only the neighbourhood of the set-point.

The material entering the step is defined by the capture step. Aggregate and charge
variants in the Protein A pool are formed upstream and are not controlled here, so the
study measures both the level in the pool and the change across the hold. Aggregate is
reduced downstream by cation exchange (PCP-007), and the charge-variant profile of the
drug substance is set in the production bioreactor (PCP-003).

## Quality attributes in scope

One drug-substance critical quality attribute is set by this step, and it is given with
its acceptance criterion and its criticality in @tbl-cqa.

: Drug-substance critical quality attribute set by the low-pH hold. {#tbl-cqa}

Enveloped-virus clearance is of very high criticality, and its acceptance criterion is
cumulative over the purification train instead of specific to any one step, so the
criterion this study must meet is the step's own contribution to that total, which is
derived in §7. Criticality is treated as a continuum under ICH Q9(R1) [@ichq9], and the
Tool #1 score in @tbl-cqa combines the impact of the attribute on safety and efficacy with the
uncertainty in that impact.

Two further attributes are governed by the step without being set by it (@tbl-cqa-hold).
Neither is cleared here. Both rise slowly during an acidic hold, so the decision rule for
each is that the pool stays inside the drug-substance specification and that the change
across the hold is characterized and bounded.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 ranked the parameters of this step before any characterization was run, and its
output is the study type in @tbl-params. The ranking combined the potential impact of a
parameter on a critical quality attribute with its potential to interact with the other
parameters, and a parameter with no data or rationale behind it was ranked at the highest
level [@amab2009].

Inactivation pH carries the highest rank at this step. Its consequence is two-sided.
Above the top of the studied range the antibody is stable but inactivation is incomplete,
and below the bottom of it the kinetics are fast but the product is at risk of
aggregating. A parameter whose failure modes lie on both sides of its range has no safe
direction in which to drift, which is why it is carried into the multivariate design and
why the criteria of §7 are applied as a pair and not one at a time.

Hold time and temperature act on the same inactivation kinetics as pH, so their effects
cannot be resolved one parameter at a time, and both are carried into the multivariate
design with pH. A-Mab concentration is ranked lower. Prior knowledge indicates that
protein concentration has little or no effect on inactivation kinetics or on aggregation
over the range the capture step delivers [@amab2009], and the concentration of the
Protein A pool is an outcome of that step and not a set-point of this one. Its normal
operating range and its characterization range therefore coincide (@tbl-params), and it
will be assessed univariately as described in §6.4.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

Virus cannot be introduced into a manufacturing facility, so the clearance study will be
executed on a scaled-down model of the hold with spiked virus. ICH Q5A(R2) requires that
such a model be shown to represent the production step before its results are applied to
that step [@ichq5a]. The qualification will be executed and documented under SOP-1001,
and its status will be stated in PCR-006 before any characterization result is reported.

The model matches the commercial step on the variables that govern inactivation. Control
of pH, hold temperature, hold time, mixing and the surface-to-volume ratio of the
vessel are matched or bracketed, and the titration profile is reproduced so that the pool
reaches the target pH over a comparable time, since the titration itself is part of the
exposure the virus receives. Scale-independent variables are operated at the values
proposed for commercial manufacture, and scale-dependent variables are set so
that the small-scale hold reproduces the performance of the full-scale hold. Qualification
compares the pH trajectory after titration, the temperature profile over the hold, and
the change in aggregate and charge variants across the hold, against the corresponding
at-scale data from clinical and engineering batches. The comparison and its acceptance
criteria are held in the qualification record under SOP-1001.

The spiking arrangement is part of the model and is qualified with it. Virus stock will
be added to the load in a proportion small enough that the composition of the load is not
materially altered, and the spiked load will be sampled before titration to fix the input
titre of that run. Cytotoxicity and interference controls will be run on every matrix
presented to the infectivity assay, and hold samples will be neutralized on withdrawal so
that inactivation does not continue in the sample. A spike large enough to change the
load, or a matrix that suppresses the assay, would bias the log reduction factor upward,
so these controls are what bound that risk and their results will be reported with the
clearance data in PCR-006.

Replicated centre-point runs are the source of the pure-error estimate used in the
lack-of-fit test (§5.5). The screening design carries `{python} c_scr` centre points and
the response-surface design carries `{python} c_rsm`.

## Operation

The step will be operated at small scale in the sequence used at commercial scale, under
SOP-2009. The spiked load is titrated with acid to the inactivation pH, mixed to
homogeneity, and held at the target temperature for the target time. The pool is then
titrated to the load condition of the cation exchange step and filtered. Samples are
drawn as described in §5.4.

Inputs controlled to platform specification are not characterized in this study. Buffer
and titrant composition, vessel material, mixing rate and filter type are fixed at their
platform settings, are covered by identity and quality control, and are held constant
across every run of the design. Varying them would confound the parameters the study is
built to resolve.

## Analytical methods

The validated methods that carry the study are listed with the other controlled
documents in @tbl-sop. XMuLV infectivity is measured as a fifty-percent tissue culture
infectious dose (TCID50) under AMV-3017, aggregate by size-exclusion chromatography under
AMV-3011, and acidic charge variants by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing under
AMV-3013, and each method is validated for the neutralized hold pool as well as for the
load presented to the step.

The log reduction factor is the difference between the log₁₀ total infectivity of the
spiked load and the log₁₀ total infectivity of the held pool, with the volume of each
taken into account. Method performance, including the limit of detection that bounds the
largest reduction the assay can report, is held in the validation records named in
@tbl-sop and is summarized in PCR-006. Where a pool sample gives no detectable virus, the
reduction will be reported as at least the value calculated from the detection limit, and
that run will not be treated as a point estimate of the reduction achieved.

## Sampling plan

Every run gives a spiked load sample and an end-of-hold pool sample, and both are assayed
for infectivity, for aggregate and for charge variants. The load sample fixes the input
titre and the input quality of the run, so each run carries its own control and the
reduction is calculated within the run. Load attributes (aggregate, acidic variants and protein
concentration) are recorded for every run, so that a load outside its usual composition can be identified afterwards.

Time-course samples will be drawn at intermediate points during the hold on the
centre-point runs. These samples confirm the shape of the inactivation curve and show
whether the reduction is complete before the end of the shortest hold in the design,
which is the question a hold-time range answers only indirectly. Samples are neutralized
on withdrawal and handled under SOP-2009, and identity, time of withdrawal and analyst
are recorded at the point of collection (§9).

## Statistical methods

The analysis follows SOP-1002. Each parameter is coded so that the low and high edges of
its characterization range take the coded levels -1 and +1 and the midpoint takes the
coded level 0. Coding puts parameters measured in different units on a common scale, so
that the estimated effects can be compared directly. The screening data will be fitted by
ordinary least squares with all main effects and all two-factor interactions, and an
effect will be reported as twice the corresponding coded coefficient. Significance is
judged at α = 0.05.

The response-surface data will be fitted with the full quadratic model in the
multivariate parameters. Model adequacy will be judged on the coefficient of
determination, on its adjusted and predicted forms, on the overall F test, and on an
analysis of variance that partitions the residual variation into lack of fit and pure
error from the replicated centre points. A model whose lack of fit is significant at
α = 0.05 will not be used to define the operating region, and both the deficiency and the
action taken in response will be reported in PCR-006.

The two designs do different work. The screening design identifies which parameters and
which interactions are active over the ranges studied. The response-surface model is the
predictive model, and it is the basis of the operating region, of the proven acceptable
ranges of §8 and of any prediction at a condition the design did not run. No design-space
claim will be made from the screening fit.

Commercial-scale capability will be estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches, with the parameters drawn from their normal
operating ranges and propagated through the fitted response-surface model. It will be
reported in PCR-006 as a one-sided capability index against each criterion of @tbl-acc.
The capability estimate informs the control strategy, and this plan sets no numeric
capability threshold as a condition of the study.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

The parameters of the step, their set-points, their characterization ranges, their normal
operating ranges and their study type are given in @tbl-params.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO))
```

: Parameters to be studied, with their characterization and normal operating ranges. {#tbl-params}

Every characterization range is wider than the range the process is controlled to. The
ranges are expanded beyond the normal operating ranges so that the study describes the
step at conditions the process will not normally see, which is what allows a future
excursion to be assessed against data instead of against judgement at the time it occurs.
The expansion is not symmetric, because the risk that each edge represents is not symmetric.

The pH range is the narrowest of the multivariate ranges in relative terms, and each of its edges is
placed by a different mechanism. The upper edge is set where incomplete inactivation
becomes the limiting concern, since the reduction achieved falls as pH rises. The lower
edge is set above the pH at which acid-induced aggregation of the platform antibodies has
been observed [@amab2009], so that the study bounds the product-quality risk without
running into it. Hold time is expanded upward only. A hold shorter than the routine
minimum is not a condition the procedure permits, and the case that needs bounding is the
hold extended by an interruption downstream. Temperature brackets its normal operating
range on both sides, at the limits to which the jacket of the temperature-controlled hold
vessel can be set (§5.2).

The letter codes used in the design matrices and in the analysis are given in
@tbl-legend.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
```

: Factor legend for the coded design matrices. {#tbl-legend}

## Screening design

The screening study is a full two-level factorial in the `{python} n_fac` multivariate
parameters with `{python} c_scr` centre points, giving `{python} n_scr` runs. A full
factorial estimates every main effect and every two-factor
interaction without aliasing, so no effect the study is interested in is confounded with
another, and the three-factor interaction, which prior knowledge gives no reason to
expect, is the only term left in the residual. The centre points give a direct estimate
of pure error and an indication of curvature. The run order will be randomized, and the
planned coded matrix is given in Appendix A.

The screening study identifies which parameters and interactions are active over the
ranges studied. It does not define an operating region, and no range will be justified
from it alone.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study is a face-centred central composite design in the same
`{python} n_fac` parameters, with `{python} n_fact_runs` factorial runs,
`{python} n_axial_runs` axial runs and `{python} c_rsm` centre points, giving
`{python} n_rsm` runs. The axial runs sit on the faces of the design cube, so the design
adds the curvature terms without going outside the characterization ranges of
@tbl-params. Each parameter is observed at its low edge, its midpoint and its
high edge, which is what the estimate of a quadratic term requires.

Every screening parameter will be carried into the response-surface design whatever the
screening outcome. The design is small, a parameter dropped after screening cannot
contribute a curvature term or an interaction to the predictive model, and the cost of
carrying a parameter that turns out to be inactive is a few runs against the cost of a
second execution. The planned coded matrix is given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

A-Mab concentration will be assessed one parameter at a time, at the low, middle and high
points of its characterization range, with the other parameters held at their
set-points. These runs are spiked, sampled and assayed exactly as the multivariate runs
are. The assessment answers a single question, which is whether the log reduction factor
and the change in aggregate across the hold are constant over the concentration range the
capture step delivers.

A null result is an outcome and not a gap. If concentration has no measurable effect on
either response, the parameter will be classified on that evidence in PCR-006, its full
characterization range will be carried forward as an acceptable range, and the runs will
remain in the knowledge space as evidence that the step is insensitive to it.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

The study passes when the criteria of @tbl-acc are met simultaneously over a
contiguous region of the multivariate parameters. Meeting them individually at
different conditions is not a pass, because the process must satisfy all of them at
whatever condition it is run.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(acceptance_df())
```

: Acceptance criteria for the measured responses, with the basis of each. {#tbl-acc}

The clearance criterion is a floor, and it is derived rather than specified. The
drug-substance requirement for enveloped virus is cumulative over the purification train
and is given in @tbl-cqa as at least `{python} f"{xmulv_cum:g}"` log₁₀. The anion exchange
and small-virus retentive filtration steps (Steps 8 and 9) are credited with defined
contributions to that total in the modular claim, and subtracting those contributions
from the cumulative requirement leaves what this step must deliver on its own. The resulting floor is
`{python} f"{acc_xmulv:.2f}"` log₁₀, and every condition inside the operating region must
meet it.

The clearance criterion is applied to the mean response predicted by the model. A
response surface predicts mean levels, so a region drawn on the mean alone offers only
even odds of meeting the criterion at its own edge. The region will therefore be reported
twice, once on the mean prediction and once with a prediction interval applied, and the
second of these is the region that supports the control strategy, because the control
strategy has to hold for a batch and not for the average of many batches. The interval
accounts for process variation, for assay variation and for the uncertainty of the fitted model
itself.

The remaining criteria are ceilings taken directly from the drug-substance
specifications. The step is credited with no reduction of either attribute, so the
decision rule is that the pool stays inside its specification everywhere in the region
and that the change across the hold is quantified against the load. An increase that
remains inside the specification is an acceptable outcome, and it will be reported with
its magnitude and not only with its disposition.

Model adequacy is a precondition of the operating region and not a criterion applied to
the process. The region will be declared from the response-surface model only where the
lack-of-fit test is not significant at α = 0.05 and the predicted coefficient of
determination supports prediction and not merely description. Where a response fails that
test, the range for the parameters governing it will be set from the observed data at the
design points, and the limitation will be stated in PCR-006.

Two outcomes end the study without an operating region. If no contiguous set of
conditions satisfies every criterion at once, the ranges will be re-cut and the study
repeated under a revised plan. If the scale-down model fails its qualification, no result from the
study will be used, and the failure will be reported under SOP-1001.

Meeting the step criterion does not establish the viral safety of the drug substance.
The cumulative claim is assembled in PCMR-001 from this step, from PCR-008 and from
PCR-009, and the argument that the contributing mechanisms are orthogonal is made there.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

A proven acceptable range will be reported for each governed attribute and each of the
multivariate parameters. The acceptance basis is the one used in §7. For aggregate
and acidic variants it is the drug-substance specification, and for enveloped-virus
clearance it is the back-calculated step floor of @tbl-acc.

Two analyses will be run for every pair of parameter and attribute. The first holds the
other parameters at their set-points and scans the parameter of interest across its
characterization range. The second propagates the normal operating ranges of the other
parameters, drawing each of them at random inside its own range and evaluating the fitted
response-surface model at every point of the scan. The scan uses `{python} D.PAR_GRID`
grid points across the characterization range and `{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"` draws at
each grid point, under a fixed random seed so that the analysis reproduces exactly.

The second analysis is the reproducible default for the control strategy. It answers the
question a manufacturing deviation actually raises, which is whether one parameter is
acceptable while everything else sits somewhere inside its own range instead of at a
nominal value. The first analysis is retained because it isolates the parameter, and the
difference between the two is a direct measure of how much the other parameters matter.

The decision rule is the same in both analyses. The proven acceptable range of a
parameter is the contiguous interval around the set-point over which the predicted
response stays inside its acceptance criterion, and it is reported in the units of the
parameter. Where both analyses give the same interval and that interval covers the whole
characterization range, the parameter is acceptable everywhere it was studied and is also
insensitive to co-variation of the others inside their normal operating ranges, as far as
the fitted model can show. Where the propagated interval is narrower, the attribute that binds it will be named and the
residual margin to the criterion will be given.

Each governed attribute will be reported with a figure that plots the response against
its governing parameter, with the acceptance limit drawn, the acceptable region shaded,
and the set-point and the normal operating range marked. The two analyses are the two
panels of that figure.

A proven acceptable range and an operating region answer different questions. A proven
acceptable range is a statement about one parameter under stated conditions for the
others. The region of §7 is multivariate. Where every proven acceptable range covers the
whole characterization range, the constraint that binds routine operation is a corner of
that region and not any single parameter, and PCR-006 will say which corner it is.

# Data management and integrity

Study data will be recorded, reviewed and retained under the site data-integrity
procedures, and every record will be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and
accurate, as well as complete, consistent, enduring and available. Raw analytical data
remain in the validated systems of the analytical laboratory. The design, the run order,
the fitted models and the derived ranges are held in the statistical environment
identified in SOP-1002, together with the seed and the script that reproduce them.

Each dataset is reviewed by a second qualified person before it is analysed, and the
analysis is checked against the raw records before PCR-006 is issued. Any correction to a
recorded value carries its reason, its author and its date, and the original value stays
legible.

# Roles and responsibilities

The study is executed by Process Development at the sending site, with the analytical and
virological work performed by the functions named in @tbl-roles. Each function approves
the part of the plan it will execute.

| Function | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Process Development / MSAT | Owns this plan, executes the scale-down runs, analyses the data and authors PCR-006. |
| Analytical Development | Performs the size-variant and charge-variant assays and maintains their validated status. |
| Virology laboratory | Prepares and titrates the virus stock, performs the infectivity assay and runs the cytotoxicity and interference controls. |
| Manufacturing Science | Confirms that the scale-down model represents the commercial step and reviews the proposed operating ranges. |
| Statistics | Approves the designs, the analysis and the model-adequacy assessment. |
| Quality Assurance | Approves this plan and PCR-006 and dispositions any deviation from the plan. |

: Functions and their responsibilities for the study. {#tbl-roles}

A departure from this plan is raised, investigated and dispositioned under the site
deviation procedure. Every deviation is reported in PCR-006 with its investigation, its
root cause where one is established, and its assessed impact on the conclusions of the
study.

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-006. That report gives the qualification status of
the scale-down model, the screening and response-surface results, the operating region,
the proven acceptable ranges, the parameter classifications and the step's contribution
to the control strategy. It rolls up into PCMR-001.

The study runs in four phases. The scale-down model is qualified first, and no
characterization run starts before its qualification is accepted. The screening study
runs next. The response-surface study and the univariate assessment follow, and they may
run in parallel where virus stock and assay capacity allow. Analysis and reporting follow
the last analytical result. No calendar dates are fixed in this plan, and the campaign
schedule is held under PCMP-001.

# Risks and assumptions

The study rests on four assumptions, and each one carries a risk to the conclusions drawn
from it.

- The scale-down model represents the commercial hold. This is the largest assumption in
  the study, because every range it justifies is applied at commercial scale, and it is
  managed by the qualification described in §5.1 and by the comparison against the
  clinical and engineering data at scale that PCR-006 will present.
- The spiked load behaves like the unspiked pool. A virus spike adds material the
  commercial process does not contain, and the spike proportion is held low and
  controlled for that reason. A residual assumption remains, and it is stated as a
  limitation of the clearance claim in PCR-006.
- The load entering the step is representative of routine capture material. Aggregate and
  charge variants are formed upstream, so a load outside its usual composition would move
  the pool results without any parameter of this step changing. Load attributes are
  recorded on every run so that the assumption can be tested after the fact.
- The fitted model holds only inside the characterization ranges. No prediction will be
  made outside them, and operation outside them is a change managed under the quality
  system and not a movement supported by this study.

Two further risks are practical. Virus stock and infectivity-assay capacity (shared with
the studies of PCP-008 and PCP-009) set the rate at which runs can be executed, and a failed assay costs a repeat of the analysis and, in
the worst case, of the run. Availability of representative Protein A pool material is the
second constraint, and the study will use material pooled from more than one upstream
batch where a single batch is insufficient. Both risks affect the schedule of the study
and neither affects its conclusions.

# Approvals

This plan takes effect when the approvers named in @tbl-appr have signed it. No
characterization run under it may start before that date. Any change to the design, to
the ranges or to the acceptance criteria requires the same approvals as the original
plan, and the change is recorded before the affected runs are executed.
